title: Dilation calculus for currents in ℝ^P (existence, boundary, integer multiplicity, representations, mass, Hausdorff scaling)
statement: For a ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 let η(y) := dilation a λ y = λ⁻¹(y − a); X' ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) is called a dilation of X ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) if X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω') for all test m-forms ω, ω' on ℝ^P with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y. Let P, m ∈ ℕ, a ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0. Then (1) every X ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) has a dilation X'; (2) if X' is a dilation of X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P), then ∂X'(ω) = λ^{−m}∂X(ω') whenever ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for all y (∂X' is a dilation of ∂X); (3) a dilation of an integer multiplicity current is integer multiplicity; (4) if X' is a dilation of X and X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for all ω (μ a Borel measure, ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_m(ℝ^P)), then X'(ω) = ∫ξ(a + λy)(ω(y)) d(λ^{−m}·η_*μ)(y) for all ω; (5) if X' is a dilation of X then M_{η(W)}(X') = λ^{−m}M_W(X) for every W ⊆ ℝ^P; (6) Hᵐ(η(A)) = λ^{−m}Hᵐ(A) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P (Hᵐ = μHE[m]).
